title: Cap. III Rej. Rat. 1: Vasquez infants — deny invented common good-pleasure will
pass_a_gloss: Vasquez himself, forced before the evidence of the matter, grants us that to certain little ones not even a sufficient remedy through Christ could have been applied by human diligence. I add, nor was it applied by Divine providence. And hence from the posterior we gather that God did not have this common will of good pleasure of saving all and each which they invent. Finally, what most of all cuts the nerves of the proposed argumentation: I deny that that will of God which before the foreknowledge of merits decreed to give eternal life to the elect was only this common, inefficacious [will], and what they call [a will] of simple affection or complacency; and I affirm that it was a certain special and most efficacious will.
pass_b_english: Even Vasquez, pressed by the facts, grants that for some infants no sufficient Christ-remedy could be applied by human care. I add: nor was it applied by divine providence. So a posteriori God never had that invented common good-pleasure will to save every single person. Finally — and this most cuts their argument's nerve — I deny that the will by which God, before foreknowledge of merits, decreed eternal life for the elect was only that common, inefficacious "simple affection / complacency" will; I affirm it was a special, most efficacious will.
source_text: Ipse Vasques ante rei evidentiam coactus, concedit nobis, quibusdam parvulis nec sufficiens remedium per Christum humana diligentia potuisse applicari. Ego addo, nec Divina providentia fuisse applicatum. Atque hinc a posteriori colligimus, Deum non habuisse hanc communem, quam comminiscuntur, salvandi omnes & singulos beneplaciti voluntatem. Postremo, quod maxime facit ad argumentationis propositae nervos incidendos, nego illam Dei voluntatem, quae ante praescientiam meritorum decrevit dare vitam aeternam electis, fuisse solummodo hanc communem, inefficacem, & quam vocant, simplicis affectus sive complacentiae; atque affirmo fuisse specialem quandam & efficacissimam voluntatem.
